source_caption:
To prepare for Malcolm X, Denzel Washington studied Malcolm’s speeches for months and even visited Mecca, mirroring part of the civil rights leader’s own journey. His performance was so powerful that many viewers felt they were watching Malcolm himself on screen.

Malcolm X (1992), directed by Spike Lee, starring Denzel Washington, Angela Bassett, Delroy Lindo. A sweeping and powerful biographical epic that traces the transformation of one of the most influential figures in American history, exploring identity, justice, and the fight for civil rights.

source_details.synopsis: Malcolm X is a 1992 American epic biographical drama film about the civil rights activist Malcolm X. Directed and co-written by Spike Lee, the film stars Denzel Washington in the title role, alongside Angela Bassett, Albert Hall, Al Freeman Jr., and Delroy Lindo. Lee has a supporting role, while Black Panther Party co-founder Bobby Seale, the Rev. Al Sharpton, and future South African president Nelson Mandela make cameo appearances. The screenplay, co-credited to Lee and Arnold Perl, is based largely on Alex Haley's 1965 book The Autobiography of Malcolm X.
